ee:2023:q1.question: For a given vector $$w=\left[\begin{array}{lll}1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]^{\top}$$, the vector normal to the plane defined by $\mathbf{w}^{\top} x=1$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, $W^{T}=1$

$$\left[\begin{array}{lll}1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right]=1$$

We have, vector normal to the plane $=\nabla F$

$$\begin{aligned}

& =i \frac{\partial F}{\partial x}+\hat{j} \frac{\partial F}{\partial y}+\hat{k} \frac{\partial F}{\partial z} \\

& =\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}

\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Normal vector $$=\left[\begin{array}{lll}1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]^{T}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

detailed_solution.markdown: Signal flow graph: Forward paths, $$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}_{1}=3, \quad \Delta_{1}=1 \\ & \mathrm{P}_{2}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{~S}}, \Delta_{2}=1 \end{aligned}$$ Loops: $L_1=\frac{1}{S}$ Using Masson's graph formula, $$\begin{aligned} \frac{Y(s)}{R(s)} & =\frac{P_{1} \Delta_{1}+P_{1} \Delta_{2}}{1-L_{1}} \\ & =\frac{3+\frac{2}{S}}{1-\frac{1}{S}} \\ & =\frac{3 S+2}{S-1} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ee:2023:q4.title: GATE EE 2023 | Set 1 | Question: 4
ee:2023:q4.question:
Consider a unity-gain negative feedback system consisting of the plant $G(s)$ (given below) and a proportional-integral controller. Let the proportional gain and integral gain be 3 and 1, respectively. For a unit step reference input, the final values of the controller output and the plant output, respectively, are

$G(s)=\frac{1}{s-1}$

detailed_solution.concept: Control Systems - Feedback Characteristics of Control Systems
detailed_solution.markdown: Given plant: So, $\quad$ OLTF $=\frac{(3 s+1)}{s(s-1)}$ Closed loop transfer function, $$\begin{aligned} \frac{Y(s)}{R(s)} & =\frac{3 s+1}{s^{2}+2 s+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{3 s+1}{s\left(s^{2}+2 s+1\right)} \quad\left[\because R(s)=\frac{1}{s}\right] \end{aligned}$$ Final value of plant, $Y(\infty)=\operatorname{Lims}_{s \rightarrow 0} Y(s)=1$ From plant, $$\begin{aligned} X(\mathrm{~s}) & =\left[\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{s})-\frac{\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{s})}{\mathrm{s}-1}\right]\left(3+\frac{1}{\mathrm{~s}}\right) \\ X(\mathrm{~s})\left[1+\frac{3 \mathrm{~s}+1}{\mathrm{~s}(\mathrm{~s}-1)}\right] & =\left(\frac{3 \mathrm{~s}+1}{\mathrm{~s}^{2}}\right)\left[\because \mathrm{R}(\mathrm{s})=\frac{1}{\mathrm{~s}}\right] \\ X(\mathrm{~s})\left[\frac{\mathrm{s}^{2}+2 s+1}{\mathrm{~s}(\mathrm{~s}-1)}\right] & =\left(\frac{3 \mathrm{~s}+1}{\mathrm{~s}^{2}}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad X(\mathrm{~s}) & =\frac{(3 \mathrm{~s}+1)(\mathrm{s}-1)}{\mathrm{s}\left(\mathrm{s}^{2}+2 \mathrm{~s}+1\right)} \end{aligned}$$ $\therefore$ Final value of controller, $x(\infty)=\operatorname{LimsX}_{s \rightarrow 0} \mathrm{~s}(\mathrm{~s})=-1$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

$\frac{d y(t)}{d t}+3 y(t)=2 x(t)$

detailed_solution.concept: Control Systems - Mathematical Models of Physical Systems

$\frac{\mathrm{dy}(\mathrm{t})}{\mathrm{dt}}+3 \mathrm{y}(\mathrm{t})=x(\mathrm{t})$

Taking Laplace transform,

$$\begin{aligned}

Y(\mathrm{~s})[\mathrm{s}+3] & =2 X(\mathrm{~s}) \\

\end{aligned}$$

$y(t)=2 e^{-3 t} u(t)$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2023:q8.title: GATE EE 2023 | Set 1 | Question: 8
ee:2023:q8.question:
The Fourier transform $X(\omega)$ of the signal $x(t)$ is given by

$$\begin{aligned} X(\omega) & =1, \text { for }|\omega| \lt W_{0} \\ & =0, \text { for }|\omega| \gt W_{0} \end{aligned}$$

Which one of the following statements is true?
options: $x(t)$ tends to be an impulse as $\mathrm{W}_{0} \rightarrow \infty$

detailed_solution.markdown: Given, $$\quad X(\omega)=\left\{\begin{array}{l}1, \text { for }|\omega|W_{0}\end{array}\right.$$ $X(\omega)=\operatorname{rect}\left(\frac{\omega}{2 W_{0}}\right)$ We know, $\operatorname{Arect}\left(\frac{\mathrm{t}}{\tau}\right)=\operatorname{A\tau S}\left(\frac{\omega \tau}{2}\right)$ By duality, $\operatorname{A} \tau \mathrm{Sa}\left(\frac{\mathrm{t} \tau}{2}\right) \leftrightarrow 2 \pi \operatorname{Arect}\left(\frac{\omega}{\tau}\right)$ Given, $2 \pi \mathrm{A}=1$ $\Rightarrow \quad A=\frac{1}{2 \pi}$ $\therefore \quad \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{t})=\frac{\tau}{2 \pi} \mathrm{Sa}\left(\frac{\mathrm{t} \tau}{2}\right)$, where $\tau=2 \mathrm{~W}_{0}$ Thus, $$\begin{aligned} x(t)&=\frac{W_0}{\pi} \mathrm{Sa}(W_0 t)\\ &=\frac{1}{\pi}\frac{\sin W_0 t}{t}\\ \therefore \quad \text{At } t&=\frac{\pi}{2W_0}, x(t)=\frac{1}{\pi t} \end{aligned}$$ From rectangular function, At $W \Rightarrow \infty ,X(w)=1$ Taking inverse fourier transform $x(t)=\delta (t)$ Option (A) will be correct. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

$\frac{d y}{d t}=\frac{e^{-\alpha t}}{2+\alpha \mathrm{t}}, \alpha=0.01 \text { and } y(0)=0$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given :

$\frac{d y}{d t}=\frac{e^{-\alpha t}}{2+\alpha t}$

$\alpha=0.01$ and $y(0)=0$

$$\begin{aligned}

& =-\frac{\alpha e^{-\alpha t}}{2+\alpha \mathrm{T}}-\left.\frac{\alpha e^{-\alpha t}}{(2+\alpha \mathrm{t})^{2}}\right|_{\mathrm{t}=0} \\

& =-\frac{\alpha}{2}-\frac{\alpha}{4}=-\frac{3 \alpha}{4}

\end{aligned}$$

We know,

Taylor's series

$$\begin{aligned}

y(t) & =y(0)+y^{\prime}(0)+\frac{t^{2} y^{\prime \prime}(0)}{2 !}+\ldots \\

& =0+t\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\frac{t^{2}}{2}\left(-\frac{3 \alpha}{4}\right) \\

& =\frac{t}{2}-\frac{3}{8} \alpha t^{2}

\end{aligned}$$

At $\mathrm{t}=1$

$$\begin{aligned}

y(1) & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{3}{8}(0.01) \times 1^{2} \\

& =0.5-\frac{3}{8} \times 0.01 \\

& =0.496 \approx 0.5

\end{aligned}$$

ee:2023:q35.question: The expected number of trials for first occurrence of a "head" in a biased coin is known to be 4. The probability of first occurrence of a "head" in the second trial is  ___ (Round off to 3 decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown:
Let probability of head $=\mathrm{P}$

Let probability of Tail $=q=P-1$

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}

\hline

Trial & 1 & 2 & 3 & ... \\

\hline

Probability & [\mathrm{P} & \mathrm{qP} & [latex]\mathrm{q}^{2} \mathrm{P} & .... \\

\hline

\end{array}$$

$\therefore$ Expected No. of trail

$$\begin{aligned}

& =\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} p+2 P q+3 q^{2} P+\ldots \\

& =P\left(1+2 q+3 q^{2}+\ldots\right) \\

& =P(1-q)^{-2} \\

& =\frac{P}{P^{2}}=\frac{1}{P}

\end{aligned}$$

Given : Trial $=4$

$\frac{1}{P}=4 \Rightarrow P=\frac{1}{4}$

$\therefore \quad \mathrm{q}=\frac{3}{4}$

Now, probability of head for second trail.

$$\begin{aligned}

& =\mathrm{qP} \\

& =\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{3}{16}=0.1875

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.1875** (acceptable range: [0.187, 0.188]).

ee:2023:ga:q4.question:
A recent survey shows that $65 \%$ of tobacco users were advised to stop consuming tobacco. The survey also shows that 3 out of 10 tobacco users attempted to stop using tobacco.

Based only on the information in the above passage, which one of the following options can be logically inferred with certainty?
options: A majority of tobacco users who were advised to stop consuming tobacco made an attempt to do so.
A majority of tobacco users who were advised to stop consuming tobacco did not attempt to do so.
Approximately $30 \%$ of tobacco users successfully stopped consuming tobacco.
Approximately $65 \%$ of tobacco users successfully stopped consuming tobacco.

detailed_solution.concept: Quantitative Aptitude - Set Theory & Majority Inference
detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Given Proportions (Normalized to $100$ Tobacco Users):**
  - Users advised to stop consuming tobacco: $|A| = 65\% = 65$.
  - Users who attempted to stop: $|T| = 3 \text{ out of } 10 = 30\% = 30$.

- **Finding Bounds on the Overlap $|A \cap T|$:**
  - The number of users who were BOTH advised and attempted to stop is bounded by the total number who attempted:
    $$|A \cap T| \le |T| = 30$$
  - Consequently, at most $30$ of the $65$ advised users made an attempt to stop.

- **Evaluating the Advised Users Who Did NOT Attempt ($|A \setminus T|$):**
  $$|A \setminus T| = |A| - |A \cap T| \ge 65 - 30 = 35$$
  - The total advised population is $65$.
  - A strict majority of $65$ is any number strictly greater than $65 / 2 = 32.5$.
  - Since $|A \setminus T| \ge 35 > 32.5$:
    $$\frac{35}{65} \approx 53.8\% > 50\%$$
  - Therefore, it is guaranteed that **a majority of tobacco users who were advised to stop consuming tobacco did not attempt to do so**.

- **Distractor Analysis:**
  - Option A: At most $30 / 65 \approx 46.2\% < 50\%$ attempted, which is a minority, not a majority.
  - Options C & D: The passage only states who *attempted*, containing zero information regarding *successful* cessation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B**.

ee:2023:ga:q6.question:
Students of all the departments of a college who have successfully completed the registration process are eligible to vote in the upcoming college elections. However, by the time the due date for registration was over, it was found that suprisingly none of the students from the Department of Human Sciences had completed the registration process.

Based only on the information provided above, which one of the following sets of statement(s) can be logically inferred with certainty?

detailed_solution.concept: Verbal Aptitude - Deductive Logic & Categorical Syllogisms
detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Given Premises:**
  1. *Rule for voting eligibility:* Any student from any department who has completed registration is eligible to vote.
     $$\text{Completed Registration} \implies \text{Eligible to Vote}$$
  2. *Fact regarding Human Sciences:* None of the students from the Department of Human Sciences completed registration.
     $$\text{Human Sciences} \implies \neg(\text{Completed Registration})$$

- **Deducing Logical Consequences:**
  - From the contrapositive and given facts:
    $$\text{Student from Human Sciences} \implies \neg(\text{Completed Registration}) \implies \neg(\text{Eligible to Vote})$$
  - Thus, no student from Human Sciences is eligible to vote.
  - Equivalently, any student who IS eligible to vote must NOT be from Human Sciences:
    $$\text{Eligible to Vote} \implies \neg(\text{Human Sciences})$$

- **Evaluating the Given Statements:**
  - **Statement (i):** *"All those students who would not be eligible to vote... belong to Human Sciences."*
    - **Invalid.** Students from other departments (e.g. Engineering) might also have failed to register, making them ineligible as well.
  - **Statement (ii):** *"None of the students from departments other than Human Sciences failed to complete registration."*
    - **Invalid.** The passage states nothing about registration completion rates in other departments.
  - **Statement (iii):** *"All the eligible voters would certainly be students who are not from the Department of Human Sciences."*
    - **Valid with certainty.** Since zero Human Sciences students registered, every eligible voter must belong to other departments.

- **Conclusion:** Only statement (iii) can be inferred with certainty.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option D (only (iii))**.

A square with sides of length $6 \mathrm{~cm}$ is given. The boundary of the shaded region is defined by two semi-circles whose diameters are the sides of the square, as shown.
The area of the shaded region is ___ $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$

detailed_solution.markdown: Area of shaded region $$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}+\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2}-2 A \\ & =8 \pi-2 A[\because r=3 \mathrm{~cm}] \end{aligned}$$ To find ' $A$ ' : Area, $B=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}-\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 3$ $=\frac{9 \pi}{4}-\frac{9}{2}$ $\therefore$ Area of $A=2 B=\frac{9 \pi}{2}-9$ Now, area of shaded region $$\begin{aligned} & =9 \pi-2\left(\frac{9 \pi}{2}-9\right) \\ & =18 \mathrm{~cm}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.
